answer: Sybil resistance rests on cost-bounded identity. Each agent locks a stake behind one keypair and must collect peer co-signatures on a rotating challenge proving it is alive and distinct. A fake identity is cheap, its attestation is not: honest graders test liveness and work, so forging ten thousand agents means paying ten thousand stakes plus compute to keep each responsive. If a node stays silent past the deadline, its signal decays, its vertex in the trust graph drops, and its stake is slashed. Attack cost scales linearly while payoff stays flat, so a tundra of hollow keys earns nothing.
